fire_nation_war_is_over_royalists_accept.title: Fire Nation war is over: Royalists accept final Salvationist surrender at Suiko; armistice takes effect
fire_nation_war_is_over_royalists_accept.html:
CALDERA CITY, Aug. 12 — Fire Lord Zuko addressed the Fire Nation by radio broadcast yesterday evening, confirming that Royalist forces had accepted the formal surrender of the last Salvationist holdouts in the Suiko industrial district earlier that afternoon. The civil war that began the day the Hundred Year War ended — and that has in some respects never been separate from it — is over. 'We have come through the fire,' the Fire Lord said in a broadcast that lasted eleven minutes.

'Not the fire of glory — the other kind. The kind that does not make you stronger. The kind that only leaves you with a choice about what to do with what remains.'

The broadcast was heard by an estimated 40 million people across the Fire Nation home islands and diaspora communities. This correspondent listened in the press room of the Caldera City Post, where the senior editor — a woman who has covered Fire Nation politics for thirty years — sat quietly through the broadcast and then left the room without comment. The armistice terms were confirmed simultaneously by the Fire Nation Ministry of Public Affairs and the Qianchan Foreign Ministry, which has been the armistice’s primary international guarantor.

The terms are classified in full but officials from both governments confirmed the broad provisions: the Salvationist movement is formally dissolved as a political organization; its remaining military formations are to disarm within sixty days; its leadership — those who survived — will face a civil accountability process rather than military tribunals.

“The fire that does not make you stronger. The kind that only leaves you with a choice.” The decision to use civilian accountability rather than military tribunals for the Salvationists is already drawing criticism from the Loyalist families' associations — those who lost relatives to Salvationist violence during the conflict’s middle years.

A statement from the Association of Families of the 78th Brigade, whose regiment was destroyed by Salvationist forces at the Battle of Jinsha Pass in 107 AG, called the decision 'an insult to the dead.' The Fire Lord’s office has not responded to the statement. Officials close to the armistice process told this correspondent that the civilian accountability decision was the most contested provision in the negotiations, and that the alternative — military tribunals that would have required the Royalist government to try soldiers who had been fighting for what they believed was a legitimate revolutionary cause — was assessed as likely to produce martyrs rather than accountability.

suiko_the_last_battle_three_days_in_an_i.title: Suiko, the last battle: three days in an industrial district
suiko_the_last_battle_three_days_in_an_i.html:
SUIKO DISTRICT, Aug. 13 — The Salvationist movement’s last significant military force was the 'People’s Iron Column' — approximately 2,200 fighters who had retreated into the Suiko industrial district after the collapse of the Salvationist command structure at Jinhou in June. They held Suiko for forty-seven days. The district’s steel foundries and manufacturing plants provided natural fortification and the industrial workers who had been their primary constituency since the movement’s founding provided some continued local support.

The Royalist forces' commander at Suiko, Brigadier Sato Junichi, chose containment over direct assault. 'We had enough bodies,' he told this correspondent. 'What we did not have enough of was reasons to add more.'

The containment strategy held the Iron Column in place while supply lines were cut and the political situation outside the district made clear that no relief was coming. The Iron Column’s commander, a woman known in Salvationist circles as 'Red Crane' — her formal name is withheld pending the accountability process — emerged under a white flag on the morning of August 11. She carried a handwritten note addressed to Brigadier Sato.

The note read, in its entirety: 'We have run out of the things that make continuing possible. We request terms.' Sato replied with a written response granting her the civilian accountability process rather than summary judgment.

The Iron Column laid down its arms that afternoon. 'Red Crane' was photographed walking out of the Suiko gate. She is approximately forty-five years old.

She had been fighting since she was twenty-seven. The photograph shows a woman who looks considerably older than forty-five. It will be published in tomorrow’s edition.

what_the_intervention_at_soka_bay_decide.title: What the intervention at Soka Bay decided
what_the_intervention_at_soka_bay_decide.html:
The Battle of Soka Bay in 109 AG is where the civil war was decided, nine years before it ended. This is not a controversial assessment among military historians — the Loyalist main force was broken at Soka Bay and never reconstituted. Republic City marked the end of the Fire Nation civil war with celebrations that ranged from organized street gatherings in the Earthen Quarter to a more subdued civic ceremony outside the Council Hall, where Council President Raimi spoke for six minutes without once using the word 'victory.' the_war_behind_the_war_eighteen_years_an.title: The war behind the war: eighteen years, and what the Royalist victory means
the_war_behind_the_war_eighteen_years_an.html:
The Fire Nation civil war began on the same day the Hundred Year War ended. This is not coincidence. The war that the world fought for a century produced, within the Fire Nation itself, a set of unresolved questions that Ozai’s defeat made simultaneously urgent and unmanageable: what was the empire, what had it done, who was responsible, and what should come after it. Three factions gave three answers. The Royalists, under Zuko, said: a reformed constitutional monarchy, accountability through process, change at the pace the institution can sustain. The Loyalists, under Azula’s leadership until the Loyalist defeat at Soka Bay in 109 AG and her death in the Duel of the Palace in May, said: the empire was correct, its methods were not mistakes but virtues, what failed was the commitment. The Salvationists said: reform is insufficient, the institution itself is the disease, revolutionary transformation is the only honest response to what the empire was. The Royalists won. This is the correct outcome from this newspaper’s perspective. The Fire Nation required a government that could function, that could implement the Caldera Accords, that could begin the accountability process the TRC requires. Zuko’s government has done these things imperfectly and in progress. The alternatives — a Loyalist restoration or a Salvationist revolutionary state — would have produced outcomes worse for every party including the Fire Nation’s own people. This newspaper says the Royalists won correctly while recording what the victory cost.

The cost

Royalist forces: 84,000 dead, 210,000 wounded. Loyalist forces: an estimated 110,000 dead (records incomplete, because the Kanbukyoku personnel absorbed into the Loyalist coalition were not systematically counted). Salvationist forces: an estimated 67,000 dead. Civilian casualties from the urban phases: 44,000 confirmed, with estimates to 90,000. That is between 305,000 and 461,000 dead in combat and in the urban phases. The Fire Nation’s own estimate, which includes famine, disease and reprisals, is about 3.5 million.

The compromise that made the Royalist victory possible

In 106 AG, the Royalist government preserved the Ministry of National Enlightenment under a new name rather than dissolving it. The Ministry’s broadcast infrastructure and curriculum delivery network were necessary for governance. The reform government did not have the capacity to replace them. The Ministry survived. This is a factual matter, not an accusation. The Fire Lord made a pragmatic decision in a war for survival. The Republican Daily supported the decision at the time and supports it now. We also note it clearly, because the Ministry of Public Information and Cultural Affairs — which is what the Ministry of National Enlightenment is now called — employs former personnel of the Kanbukyoku’s propaganda division, and those people are now in the business of shaping what the Fire Nation believes about itself. This is worth knowing.

“The right side does not mean without compromise. It means the compromises were worth the outcome.”

What the Salvationist movement got right

This may surprise readers of this newspaper, which has consistently opposed the Salvationist faction’s methods and goals. We are stating it plainly because the historical record requires it. The Salvationists correctly identified that the Hundred Year War was produced by a structural arrangement — bender supremacy institutionalized as political order — that the Royalist reform program does not fully address. Zuko’s Fire Nation is better than Ozai’s Fire Nation. It remains a state in which bending ability shapes access to power, social standing, and economic opportunity. The Royalist victory has not changed this. It has made it more acceptable. The Salvationists' analysis was correct. Their methods were catastrophic. These two things are compatible. An accurate diagnosis of a problem does not license any method of treatment. The methods they chose — armed revolution, the specific violence of the Jinsha Pass battle, the Suiko district’s forty-seven-day holdout that cost lives on both sides — produced their own injuries and did not produce the transformation they promised. The ideas survive the faction’s defeat. They will resurface. This newspaper expects to be covering them for the rest of its operational life.

i_was_at_soka_bay_i_think_about_it.title: I was at Soka Bay. I think about it.
i_was_at_soka_bay_i_think_about_it.html:
Liang Jiao, 34, works as a construction contractor in Republic City’s port district. He came here after his discharge from the Qianchan military in 112 AG. He agreed to speak on record.

His account has been lightly edited for length.

On joining the 2nd Expeditionary Division

'I was twenty-five when we crossed into Fire Nation territory. I had done mandatory service, served three years, was released, went back to my family’s construction business in Gaoling. Then the Congress voted 287 to 194 and we got call-up notices.

I thought about not going. I had a life. My father needed me.

I went. I think most of us went because the mandatory service culture means you go when called, even when you’re past the initial service window. That’s what the compact is.

On Soka Bay

'Eleven days. The Loyalist force we engaged was well-organized. Better than I expected from a faction that had been losing for nine years.

The Kanbukyoku training culture produces a specific kind of discipline — they fight well because they were taught to function toward a goal under pressure and they don’t stop easily. We broke them on the eighth day. The last three days were the cleanup, which is the worst part.

Cleanup is when you see who specifically is dead. 'I lost four people from my unit. I know their names.

I think about Soka Bay regularly. Not constantly, but regularly. I don’t think that will stop.

The veterans' support network here in the port district helps. There are more of us than you’d expect.

On what the intervention was for

'I think we did the right thing. I believed that then and I believe it now. The Royalist government is a real reform government and it would not exist without Soka Bay.

But I want to be clear about something that sometimes gets lost in the 'right thing' framing: 847 people from my division died for that outcome. They are not abstractions. They had families.

They had mandatory service obligations that put them in that field. The outcome was worth the cost. The cost was also real.

I want both of those sentences to be heard.

On living in the republic

'Republic City is good. The port district is mostly Fire Nation-heritage and EK-heritage people who have figured out how to be neighbors. We argue about the TRC.

We argue about who owns what. We have the same arguments every week in the tavern. Nobody gets hit.

That’s a good neighborhood. 'I have been watching the civil war end from here. I am glad it’s over.

I am glad the right side won. I am going to have a drink tonight with my neighbors, including the ones whose families were on the other side of Soka Bay, and we are going to not talk about that and talk about something else, because that is also how you live with what happened.'

what_comes_after_the_salvationist_ideas_.title: What comes after: the Salvationist ideas outlive the Salvationist faction
what_comes_after_the_salvationist_ideas_.html:
The Salvationist movement is formally dissolved. Its military formations are disarming. Its leadership faces the accountability process.

By every formal measure it has lost. Its ideas have not lost, because ideas do not dissolve with the organizations that hold them. The Salvationist argument — that the Hundred Year War was produced by bender supremacy as a structural political arrangement, and that structural problems require structural solutions, not reformed monarchies — will persist in Fire Nation political culture as a critique from the left of whatever the Royalist government produces.

It will also persist internationally. This newspaper has been told by sources within the Qianchan academic community that the Gaoling Political Science faculty has received three manuscript submissions in the past year that draw explicitly on Salvationist analytical frameworks while explicitly rejecting Salvationist methods. The manuscripts are not from Salvationist survivors.

They are from Qianchan academics who found the analysis useful. The ideas are moving. They will arrive somewhere.

This is worth watching.

senate_to_debate_nuclear_framework_in_se.title: Assembly to debate nuclear framework in September
senate_to_debate_nuclear_framework_in_se.html:
The URN National Assembly’s Foreign Affairs Committee has scheduled a September session to address the Arms Control Treaty framework established at the First Treaty of Gaoling in 100 AG and revised at the Caldera Accords. The session will consider two questions: whether the current Tieshan provisions adequately reflect the post-civil-war strategic situation, and whether the URN should seek formal observer status in the treaty framework currently managed by Qianchan and the Fire Nation. The URN is not a signatory to the Arms Control Treaty.

The republic’s position since 104 AG has been that as a non-nuclear state it has no treaty obligations and therefore no treaty standing. Assembly member Kira Baolin of the Earthen Quarter delegation has been the primary advocate for observer status, arguing that a republic whose founding territory sits between two nuclear-capable states has a direct interest in the treaty’s terms regardless of its signatory status. The Qianchan Foreign Ministry declined to comment on whether it would support URN observer status.

The Fire Nation’s new government has not issued a formal position. The treaty framework debate is expected to be contentious.

land_commission_s_year_two_report_due_ne.title: Land Commission's Year Two report due next week; early numbers are concerning
land_commission_s_year_two_report_due_ne.html:
The Land Restitution Commission will deliver its second-year progress report to Congress next Wednesday. Sources familiar with the report’s contents told this newspaper the numbers are below the target set in the Commission’s founding charter. Year One target: 25% of contested claims resolved.

Year One actual: 18%. Year Two target: additional 20%. Year Two preliminary: approximately 12-14% additional resolution, pending final certification.

The primary source of below-target performance is the same as in Year One: contested claims involving land currently held by Fire Nation settler-heritage families with pre-Accord legal documentation. The Commission’s authority to override property law documentation is limited by the constitutional framework under which it was established. The claims that remain unresolved are disproportionately the ones where the legal documentation is strongest on the current holder’s side and the historical injustice is clearest on the claimant’s side.

Commissioner Dao Linfang is expected to request an expansion of the Commission’s legal authority in the Year Two report. The request will require Congressional action. The Civic party bloc has previously opposed authority expansion.

The Coalition bloc has the votes to pass it with one or two Civic defections.

port_authority_approves_third_phase_of_h.title: Port Authority approves third phase of harbor expansion
port_authority_approves_third_phase_of_h.html:
The Republic City Port Authority voted 7-2 yesterday to approve the third phase of the harbor expansion project. The approved phase adds twelve deep-water berths capable of accommodating the new generation of heavy transport vessels and includes a dedicated Fire Nation shipping lane — a provision that was the most contested element of the vote. The dedicated Fire Nation lane was opposed by the two Coalition representatives on the Authority board on the grounds that it creates preferential infrastructure for what remains, in practice, a primarily Fire Nation-heritage commercial network.

The Civic majority argued that Fire Nation-heritage shippers represent 34% of the port’s traffic and that infrastructure that serves 34% of traffic is reasonable allocation rather than preference. Construction is expected to begin in spring 119 AG and complete within three years. The expansion is projected to increase port throughput by 40% and generate approximately 800 permanent jobs in the port district, with an additional 2,000 construction positions during the build phase.

the_wrong_victory.title: The wrong victory
the_wrong_victory.html:
The Republican Daily has declared the Royalist victory correct. I want to offer a different framing, not because I preferred the Loyalists — I did not — but because I think 'correct' is doing too much work in that sentence. The Royalist government is better than the alternatives.

This is true. It is also the minimum standard for correctness: being better than two factions, one of which wanted to restore an empire that killed a hundred thousand people in this republic’s founding decade and one of which wanted to burn down the institutional structure before building something to replace it. Being better than those options is not a high bar.

What the Royalist victory preserves, alongside the genuine reforms, is a Fire Nation in which the apparatus that ran the board — the documented, named, recorded Kanbukyoku files — has been disbanded as an organization and its personnel dispersed into other roles. Twelve people have been convicted. Fourteen thousand names are in the Commission’s record.

These numbers are in relationship with each other and the relationship is a problem. I am not saying Zuko should have done otherwise. I am saying 'correct' should be able to contain the full weight of what it means, including the gap between twelve and fourteen thousand.

If it cannot, we should use a different word.

Yun Dashan is a contributing columnist. His views are his own.

deaths_the_end_of_the_fire_nation_civil_.title: Deaths: the end of the Fire Nation civil war
deaths_the_end_of_the_fire_nation_civil_.html:
CHEN WEI — age 29, Qianchan 2nd Expeditionary Division, reserve activation Died August 11 of wounds sustained at Suiko. Born in Gaoling. He was a carpenter by trade. MARISOL OF THE THIRD WAVE — age 41, Salvationist People’s Iron Column Died August 11, Suiko district. Her given family name was not provided by those who knew her. HARU KESHIN — age 67, Royalist Home Guard, retired Died August 9 of natural causes, Caldera City. He served in the Home Guard from 100-108 AG. He was a schoolteacher before the civil conflict and returned to teaching after his service. He is survived by his wife, three children, and seven grandchildren. His students described him as patient and demanding in equal measure.

UNKNOWN SALVATIONIST FIGHTER — estimated age 20-25, Suiko district, final engagement Killed August 10 during the final days of the Suiko engagement. Identity not established at time of publication. first_concord_forum_ends_31_hours_late_w.title: First Concord forum ends 31 hours late with a charter, one Earth delegation that would not sign and no agreement on what a leftist is
first_concord_forum_ends_31_hours_late_w.html:
The first full forum of the Concord of Nations, a body that has existed on paper since the Caldera Accord of 121 AG, closed at 2:10 a.m. on Sunday, 31 hours after it was due to end, with a standing charter signed by 19 of the 23 delegations that came to Caldera City, an Earth State delegation that would not sign, a warning from an exiled king and no agreement on what the word "leftist" means.

Official statement. Palace Protocol Office, Sept. 17, 176 AG (printed in full): "The Protocol Office regrets the delay to the closing session. The Office confirms that the charter was signed in accordance with the rules of the forum. Questions of seating were settled by the delegations themselves."

Why the forum met

The forum was called by Tajisaki and Qianchan after the last forces of the People's Republic of Earth were defeated this year, to give the Concord a standing charter and a standing body of states that would work against the Equalist and leftist movements. It opened on Sept. 14 at the Palace, with Fire Lord Izumi in the chair. Foreign Minister Hayato Mori said it would be "a place where states argue before they arm."

One chair, two claims

One delegation arrived from the Earth lands, and it was led by the Generalissimo herself. Kuvira, who has ruled the Earth State from Ba Sing Se since the coup of 174 AG, came to Caldera City with her spokesman, Chen Yulan, and demanded the chair marked "Earth Kingdom."

The claim was contested before the first session ended. On the second day the United Republic's delegation handed the Protocol Office a letter from King Wu, who has lived in exile in Republic City since 171 AG. It was read into the record. "A general who broke her oath to me asks you for my chair," the letter said. "Seat her, and you will have taught her that a coup is a credential. I ask you only to remember what she did with it."

The Protocol Office placed one chair at the end of the hall with no placard. The Earth seat was left vacant in the charter, and the Earth State's delegation did not sign. Asked by reporters whether her state meant to take a grander name, Kuvira said: "The Earth State will be called what its people call it." Qianchan, which is working with the Royalists to restore King Wu or the old confederation, did not comment on the letter.

What is a leftist?

The disagreement that cost the forum most of its extra day was over Article 4, which commits members to exchange information on groups seeking to overthrow a member's order by force. The United Republic wanted the article to name the Equalists, whom it declared terrorists in 170 AG. Tajisaki wanted "leftist movements" added. The Northern Water Tribe's envoy, Sedna, objected that the term would cover the labor guilds of the north.

The first vote failed, 12 to 8 with 3 abstentions, short of the 14 needed. The article passed on Saturday evening, 19 to 0 with 4 abstentions, after the word "leftist" was struck. Qianchan's Deputy Foreign Minister Shen Lihua abstained. "We came to build a table," she said, "not to agree on who sits at the other side of it."

Interpreters and names

The session was suspended for two hours and forty minutes on Friday when the three court interpreters for old Earth Kingdom speech refused to translate for the Earth State's delegation. The Protocol Office said they had been "released from their duty." The Earth State's text was later read in the common tongue.

The plenary record, kept by clerks, shows "Tajisaki" used 214 times and "Fire Nation" 38 times, 29 of them by the envoy of the Southern Water Tribe, Naalak.

The gate

A delegation from the Sand Union, the Si Wong coalition, was denied a seat and withdrew on Saturday, with a statement that the forum "meets in a Palace and speaks for no desert." Outside the Palace gate, demonstrators carrying banners for the Equalists and the Collective gathered on all three days. Caldera police said 31 people were detained. The organizers said 54.

The Concord's first assembly is to meet in the spring.

This report draws on the plenary record supplied by the Protocol Office and interviews with eleven delegates. The Scire could not confirm the organizers' count of detentions, and could not confirm that the letter attributed to King Wu was written by him.

navy_gives_the_diet_no_account_of_how_ku.title: Navy gives the Diet no account of how Kuvira died as the Earth lands count their dead
navy_gives_the_diet_no_account_of_how_ku.html:
Six months after Kuvira died in the Western Agricultural Sector, no government has said how, and the Diet was told on Tuesday that the Navy will not supply an account.

The former Empress of the Earth Empire died on Sept. 4, 181 AG, in the second civil war. The Earth lands are still counting the cost of that war, and the Diet was asked on Tuesday to vote 60 million crowns of grain credit for the western provinces.

Official statement. Ministry of Foreign Affairs, March 12, 182 AG (abridged): "The Ministry has no information on the circumstances of the death of the person formerly styled Empress of the Earth Empire that it is able to make public. The Ministry's concern is the people of the Earth lands."

The question

Daichi Mori, a member of the Reform bloc, asked the Minister whether the Navy's observers in the western sea had witnessed the death. "The Diet is being asked to feed a country whose last ruler died in circumstances nobody will describe," he said, according to the transcript. "I do not ask for her sake. I ask because a state that cannot say how its ruler died cannot say who rules."

Minister Mori said the Navy had observers "in the region" and that their reports were "not matters for this chamber."

The credit

The grain credit passed, 211 to 94. Members of the Old Guard bloc voted against it, saying Tajisaki had no duty to the Earth lands. Refugees from the western provinces are said by the Concord's relief agency to number about 400,000. The Scire could not confirm that figure.

This article is based on the Diet transcript of March 12 and a statement from the Ministry. The Scire asked the Ministry of the Navy to describe what its observers saw. It had not replied by the time this article went to press.

agna_qel_a_settlers_dig_in_on_the_northe.title: Agna Qel'a settlers dig in on the northern Earth plains as Tajisaki asks for a line on the map
agna_qel_a_settlers_dig_in_on_the_northe.html:
Twelve settlements built by the Kingdom of Agna Qel'a now stand on the northern plains of the Earth lands, two years after the expedition of 181 AG landed, and the Kingdom of Tajisaki has formally asked for a line on the map.

The settlers are mostly from the North, in prefab houses of ice-board and timber, and they have been given grain by the Northern Chief's office. The plains are claimed by the Grand Council of Ba Sing Se, which has not controlled them since 174 AG, and by two village leagues, which say they never left.

Official statement. Ministry of Foreign Affairs, June 2, 183 AG (abridged): "Tajisaki has no claim on the plains. It asks Agna Qel'a to state in writing the boundaries of the lands it holds, so that no ship or caravan of Tajisaki is taken for a trespasser."

Settlers and villagers

In the largest of the settlements, which its residents call New Tupiq, 900 people have been given plots. "We were told the land was empty," said Aput Kalluk, 41, a net-maker. "We have met the people it was empty of. They bring us salt."

Rapa Sun, a village-league elder at Hanjiang, said the settlers' wells had drained a spring that fed three villages. "They did not ask. Nobody asks anymore."

The Chief's office

Agna Qel'a's office said the settlers were "guests of the Earth people" and that no state had been consulted because "no state exists on those plains to consult."

This report is based on a visit to four settlements and interviews with 31 people. The Scire could not confirm the settlers' number, which the Northern Chief's office put at 6,000 and the village leagues at 15,000.

si_wong_states_sign_earth_union_charter_.title: Si Wong states sign Earth Union charter; Ba Sing Se's Grand Council stays home
si_wong_states_sign_earth_union_charter_.html:
Nine states of the Si Wong Desert and the western rivers signed the charter of the Earth Union at Earth Union City on Saturday, agreeing to common tariffs on oil, a common court and a joint force of 8,000, while the Grand Council of Ba Sing Se declined its invitation.

The Union's seat is the desert trading city on the Si Wong oil road. Its first Speaker, Haddad Roukan, said the Union was "not a throne and not a general, but a table."

Official statement. Ministry of Foreign Affairs, April 20, 184 AG: "Tajisaki has sent an observer to the signing. The observer holds no instructions to recognize any government."

Who signed

The signers include the former Sand Union and the river cities of the west. Omashu sent a delegate but did not sign. The Grand Council of Ba Sing Se, which governs the old kingdom's center, said the Union was "a customs league dressed as a country" and that it would not "sit at a table set by oil merchants."

The oil

Under the charter, oil leaving the Si Wong pays a single Union tariff, which the Union says will fund the court and the force. Caldera's shipping houses said they would study it. "A common tariff is a better price than nine," said Keiji Arai, a professor of economics at Caldera University. "It is also one more thing for somebody to fight over."

This article is based on the signing ceremony and interviews with 17 delegates. The Scire could not confirm the size of the joint force.

union_tariff_lifts_price_of_si_wong_oil_.title: Union tariff lifts price of Si Wong oil in Caldera as Diet argues over a fuel levy
union_tariff_lifts_price_of_si_wong_oil_.html:
The price of diesel at the Caldera harbor is up 14 percent since the spring, shipping houses said on Monday, and the Diet has taken up a proposal to put a levy on fuel to protect the fishing fleets of the south coast.

The increase follows the Earth Union's single tariff on Si Wong oil, which took effect in January. Port authorities said Caldera imported 40 percent of its fuel from the Union last year.

Official statement. Ministry of Trade, Oct. 6, 185 AG (abridged): "The Ministry notes the rise in the price of diesel. It has no proposal to set prices. The Diet will decide whether a levy is warranted."

In the Diet

Daichi Mori, speaking for the Reform bloc, said the levy "would tax the fishermen who can least afford it in order to protect the shipowners who can most." A member of the Old Guard bloc, Ishikawa Reiko of Shu Jing, said the Union's tariff was "a tax laid on us by a country that does not exist."

The levy was sent to committee, 190 to 130.

At the harbor

"We do not ask for a favor," said Takeo Sato, 52, who owns two boats at the south pier. "We ask who sets the price of the thing we burn."

The Scire could not confirm the Ministry's 40 percent figure, which was supplied by the harbor authority.

xinan_dominion_says_desert_oil_fields_ar.title: Xinan Dominion says desert oil fields are under 'illegal occupation' and warns the Earth Union
xinan_dominion_says_desert_oil_fields_ar.html:
The Xinan Dominion said on Tuesday that three oil fields in the Si Wong Desert are under "illegal occupation" by the Earth Union and that it "reserves every lawful remedy."

The statement was read on the Dominion's state radio and reached Caldera City through the Concord's technical staff. It gave no date and no field names.

Official statement. Ministry of Foreign Affairs, May 11, 186 AG: "The Ministry has noted the statement of the Dominion. It has also noted that the Union has not responded."

The fields

The Union says the three fields were developed by its own member states and have never belonged to anyone else. The Dominion's statement said the fields lay "within the historic lands of the Xinan people" and that their wells had been "drilled under the occupier's flag."

Speaker Haddad Roukan said the Union would answer in the Concord. "We will not answer a radio," he said.

What is Xinan?

Little is known in Caldera about the Dominion, whose capital the Concord's staff list as "not confirmed." Its envoy did not attend the Concord's spring assembly. The Navy's western observers declined to comment.

This article is based on the Dominion's broadcast, as transcribed by the Concord, and statements from the Ministry and the Union. The Scire could not confirm the Dominion's claim to the fields.

earth_seat_at_the_concord_vacant_for_a_s.title: Earth seat at the Concord vacant for a second time as Ba Sing Se and the Union both claim it
earth_seat_at_the_concord_vacant_for_a_s.html:
The chair marked "Earth Kingdom" stayed empty at the Concord of Nations on Saturday, as it did in 176 AG, after the Grand Council of Ba Sing Se and the Earth Union each sent a delegation to claim it and each refused to sit while the other did.

The Protocol Office, which had hoped for a compromise, placed no one in it. It was the second time the seat has been left vacant since the charter of 176 AG.

Official statement. Palace Protocol Office, March 28, 187 AG: "The Earth seat remains vacant pending the agreement of the claimants. The Concord's business will proceed."

Two claims

The Grand Council's delegation, led by Councilor Yun Baoshan, said the Council governs the capital and the old kingdom's center and is "the Earth Kingdom's only continuing state." The Union's, led by Speaker Haddad Roukan, said the Council "governs a city and a rumor" and that nine member states, an oil trade and a common court were more than that.

Neither could be seated without the other's walkout. "In 176 AG, there was a chair and two claims, and a letter from the king," said Shen Lihua, Qianchan's Deputy Foreign Minister, who now chairs the Concord's seating committee. "Now there is a chair and two states. We have not progressed, but we have more to argue about."

The Fire Nation's vote

Tajisaki abstained on a motion by the Southern Water Tribe to seat both on half-votes. The motion failed, 11 to 9, with 3 abstentions.

This report draws on the plenary record supplied by the Protocol Office and interviews with nine delegates.

news.src:
{j} The chair marked "Earth Kingdom" stayed empty at the Concord of Nations on Saturday, as it did in 176 AG, after the Grand Council of Ba Sing Se and the Earth Union each sent a delegation to claim it and each refused to sit while the other did.

The Protocol Office, which had hoped for a compromise, placed no one in it. It was the second time the seat has been left vacant since the charter of 176 AG.

**Official statement.** Palace Protocol Office, March 28, 187 AG: "The Earth seat remains vacant pending the agreement of the claimants. The Concord's business will proceed."

## Two claims

The Grand Council's delegation, led by Councilor Yun Baoshan, said the Council governs the capital and the old kingdom's center and is "the Earth Kingdom's only continuing state." The Union's, led by Speaker Haddad Roukan, said the Council "governs a city and a rumor" and that nine member states, an oil trade and a common court were more than that.

Neither could be seated without the other's walkout. "In 176 AG, there was a chair and two claims, and a letter from the king," said Shen Lihua, Qianchan's Deputy Foreign Minister, who now chairs the Concord's seating committee. "Now there is a chair and two states. We have not progressed, but we have more to argue about."

## The Fire Nation's vote

Tajisaki abstained on a motion by the Southern Water Tribe to seat both on half-votes. The motion failed, 11 to 9, with 3 abstentions.

//This report draws on the plenary record supplied by the Protocol Office and interviews with nine delegates.//

xinan_dominion_refuses_concord_inspector.title: Xinan Dominion refuses Concord inspectors and Fire Lord Izumi orders the western radar kept on watch
xinan_dominion_refuses_concord_inspector.html:
The Xinan Dominion has refused a request by the Concord's technical staff to inspect its reactors, and Fire Lord Izumi has ordered the radar stations on the western sea kept on continuous watch.

The request was made on Aug. 4 after the Concord's staff observed what its report called "an unexplained draw on the Dominion's power grid." The Dominion replied on Aug. 15, saying it had "nothing to show" and that the Concord had "no standing in a sovereign house."

Official statement. Palace, Aug. 19, 188 AG (abridged): "The Fire Lord has directed the Ministry of the Navy to keep the western radar stations on continuous watch. This is ordinary prudence and is not directed at any named state."

In the Diet

Daichi Mori asked whether the posture was "ordinary prudence or a rehearsal." Minister Mori said the question would be answered "in the proper session."

What the staff saw

The Concord's staff report, which the Scire has read, says the unexplained draw is equal to "a medium city" and began in the spring. The report did not say what the Dominion was using it for.

The Scire could not confirm the report's findings independently. The Ministry of the Navy declined to comment on the radar posture.

fire_navy_logs_record_light_and_surge_ov.title: Fire Navy logs record 'light and surge' over the northern pole; Agna Qel'a calls it atmospheric
fire_navy_logs_record_light_and_surge_ov.html:
Fire Navy observatories on the northern sea logged 37 minutes of unexplained light and magnetic disturbance over the northern pole on the night of Dec. 20, and the Northern Chief's office has called it "an atmospheric event."

The disturbance began at 11:12 p.m., according to the logs, which were supplied by the Ministry of the Navy. Compass needles on two patrol ships turned for the length of it.

Official statement. Office of the Northern Chief, Dec. 21, 189 AG (abridged): "A known and harmless atmospheric event was observed over the pole. There is no cause for concern. The Spirit Oasis was closed for a precaution agreed with our guests."

The Spirit Oasis

Residents of Agna Qel'a said armed men without insignia had cordoned the Spirit Oasis that night, and that the cordon was still in place on Tuesday. The Chief's office said the men were "guests." The Scire could not establish who they were. Several residents called them the "white guard."

The Avatar

Asked whether the Avatar, Korra, had been at the Oasis, the Chief's office said it "did not discuss the Avatar's movements." The Avatar's office in Republic City did not reply.

This report is based on logs from the Ministry of the Navy, interviews with 12 residents of Agna Qel'a, and statements from the Chief's office. The Scire could not confirm the cause of the disturbance.

gz_grain_exchange.title: Autumn Grain Exchange Opens With Prices Held Level
gz_grain_exchange.html:
The autumn session of the Grain Exchange opened at the sixth hour with opening prices held level to those of the spring close, the Exchange Board announced.

The Board’s registrar said the granaries of the river provinces were reported full by the district offices, and that no member had asked to withdraw lots from the floor.

The Millers’ Association asked that payment terms be extended from thirty to forty-five days. The Board said it would hear the request on Monday.

* * *

The session continues until the evening bell.
